teaser: Every GenAI founder I know is a developer and does not think so. They never saw the sausage factory. So the book may be Generation ZX Founders.
core_idea: GenAI founders already do a whole development team's jobs, often no worse than much of the industry, but do not call themselves developers because they never saw how rough new technology is inside; since people do not pick up a book addressed to a word they do not relate to, the book may be better titled Generation ZX Founders, with 'you are a developer' as the reveal at the end.

figures.caption: One GenAI founder, many roles. In the middle, the founder who says "I am not a developer, I just tell the model what to do". Around them, what they actually do every day: senior stakeholder and business owner (decides what matters and pays for it), product owner (writes the requirements), designer, developer and engineer (builds, with agents), release manager (continuous deployment), and the head of a development team (the agents). Each of those is a job title in a technology company.

The iceberg they never saw. Above the waterline, what a user of polished products sees: the interface and the demo, about 10% of the work in Joel Spolsky's 2002 estimate. Below it, what was there when those products were new: the back end and the data; versioning; validation, authentication and authorisation; resilience; the release pipeline and real users. On the left, what founders saw, such as the iPhone launched on a golden path of taps; on the right, what they meet now that they build: versioning, stability and security.
